skill.name: ultrafast
skill.description: Create and edit video from JSON documents with the ultrafast GPU engine. Add captions, animated titles, and charts, then preview and export through the ultrafast CLI or an MCP server.
skill.summary: Create, preview, and export captioned clips and animated videos with ultrafast.
skill.author: ultrafastmov

security_audit.summary: Most flags refer to Markdown links, video settings, or routine tool usage, not traversal, reconnaissance, or shell substitution. The setup guide exposes bearer tokens through command arguments and plaintext configuration, and several install examples do not pin versions. The remote workflow omits an explicit approval step before sending project data; no evidence of deliberate exfiltration or audit manipulation was found.

remediation.issue: Bearer tokens are expanded into command arguments. The Antigravity example also stores the token in plaintext.
remediation.suggestion: Use supported environment references or secure credential storage. Omit the token-based example where neither option is supported, and advise rotating credentials exposed through these commands.

remediation.issue: Install examples use mutable package, image, or plugin references.
remediation.suggestion: Provide reviewed versions, image digests, or immutable plugin revisions where supported. Ask the user before running installers or registering a plugin source.

remediation.issue: The remote workflow does not ask for approval before transmitting video documents.
remediation.suggestion: Identify the remote endpoint and the project data it will receive. Ask for approval before sending the document, assets, or batch rows, and offer local rendering.

content.user_title: Create and Edit Videos with Ultrafast
content.value_statement: Captioned clips and animated charts take time to build and revise by hand. Ultrafast lets you edit a reusable video document, preview the result, and export it in the format you need.
actual_capabilities: Build animated titles, lower thirds, and charts from editable video templates.
Reframe talking-head footage for vertical video and animate captions from timed words, SRT, or WebVTT.
Validate project settings, preview individual frames or contact sheets, and review caption contrast and social safe areas.
Render multiple versions from one document using one data row per video.
Export H.264 MP4, ProRes, transparent WebM, GIF, image sequences, or audio-only files.
limitations: Rendering requires a configured ultrafast MCP server or a local CLI with a supported GPU.
Some export formats require FFmpeg on the rendering host.
Captions require timing data. The local voiceover tool can generate timings for narration it creates.
Remote servers receive the full document and cannot access local media paths directly.

use_cases.title: Produce a Captioned Social Clip
use_cases.description: Reframe a recorded interview for vertical video and check that captions remain readable within the social safe area.

use_cases.title: Animate a Data Explainer
use_cases.description: Turn a small dataset into an animated chart with a title and labels for a presentation or training video.

use_cases.title: Render Campaign Variants
use_cases.description: Reuse one approved promo and change product names, prices, or copy for each row of a batch.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Title Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the local renderer to make a six-second title card for [event name]. Show one preview frame before exporting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Start with an animated title and no source footage.

prompt_templates.title: Caption an Interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Reframe [interview file] as a vertical clip and add captions from [subtitle file]. Use local rendering. Preview caption contrast and placement before exporting an MP4.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Edit existing footage with supplied subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Chart Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a widescreen explainer from [labels and values]. Animate a bar chart and highlight [key result]. Show a contact sheet and review the layout before exporting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Present data with animated graphics.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Campaign Videos
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved template] and [campaign data] to plan one local export per row. Preview one row per aspect ratio and estimate render time. Wait for approval before starting the batch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Check multiple variants before committing render time.

output_examples.input: Make an eight-second vertical promo with a title, a seat count, and timed captions.
output_examples.output: Example deliverable: A 1080 by 1920 MP4 with an animated title, a seat count, and highlighted captions. A contact sheet shows the layout at selected moments.

output_examples.input: Create a widescreen explainer with a speaker label and an animated bar chart.
output_examples.output: Example deliverable: A 1920 by 1080 video with a speaker name and role, followed by a chart. A preview shows the chart labels and highlighted bar.

best_practices: Preview a contact sheet after visual changes and review contrast, framing, and caption placement before export.
Choose a trusted renderer and approve any data sent to a remote service.
Review a sample for each aspect ratio and estimate render time before running a large batch.
anti_patterns: Do not report a video as rendered when only the project document exists.
Do not export transparency to H.264 MP4 or leave an opaque background in a transparent overlay.
Do not paste a bearer token into a command argument or save it in plaintext configuration.

faq.question: What do I need to render a video?
faq.answer: Use an ultrafast MCP connection or the local ultrafast CLI. Local rendering needs a supported Metal or Vulkan GPU.

faq.question: Can I edit footage I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. Reference the footage in a project and adjust its timing, framing, or color. Add an audio node if you need the source sound.

faq.question: Does the skill transcribe interviews?
faq.answer: The documented caption workflow uses timed words, SRT, or WebVTT. The local voiceover tool can create word timings for narration it generates.

faq.question: Can I export a transparent overlay?
faq.answer: Yes. Use ProRes 4444 or VP9 WebM with alpha enabled. Remove the opaque background and check a preview frame.

faq.question: How do I make several versions of one video?
faq.answer: Use one reviewed project and supply a data row per variant. Preview a sample for each aspect ratio before starting the batch.

faq.question: Where does my project data go?
faq.answer: Local rendering reads project files on the rendering machine. A remote MCP server receives the full document and uses asset identifiers or HTTPS media URLs.
